Tie fixes and budgets to measured release problems.
acceptance: The agreed suite has no unresolved critical crash, corruption, unsafe lifetime or sustained resource-growth issue.
Quantitative performance/memory budgets are established from measured baselines and enforced.
Results identify remaining limitations, exact hardware/platform coverage and failures; critical failures are fixed before release-candidate declaration.
Tests are not made to pass through widened tolerances, automatic baseline replacement or retries masking real failures.

requirements.requirement: Establish the recurring assignment workflow and handoff contract: read AGENTS/architecture/current assignment/previous handoff, verify branch/commit/worktree, preserve unrelated work, implement only the assigned increment and extend existing systems. Continue applying this contract for assignments 01-35.
acceptance: Each assignment provides one reviewable change set or PR, updates docs/public-format migration-or-rejection policy and coverage/handoff records, and states the exact next task.
Each assignment's evidence records exact commands, revision, platform, PASS/FAIL/NOT_RUN, unverified hardware and blockers; a missing device/runner is never reported PASS.
No-op APIs, fake success and silently skipped error/lifetime/cleanup behavior cannot satisfy a gate.
An assignment does not advance while its required gate is unmet; later layers connect earlier components when those layers are introduced.

requirements.requirement: Establish meaningful engine-owned unit tests, interaction/loading/callback/lifecycle integration tests, fixed seeds/controllable clocks/explicit timeouts and tiered CI. Add subsystem-specific suites in their owner assignments instead of claiming unsupported generic coverage.
acceptance: Fast CPU checks run in ordinary CI; GPU/hardware/soak/packaged checks run on appropriate named runners.

GPU validation includes Vulkan/NVRHI messages, readback checks and visual comparisons with explicit tolerances/platform baselines; approving a baseline change is intentional, never automatic failure recovery.
Audio qualification includes both offline/null-device and real-device checks, with their conclusions kept distinct.
Tests avoid arbitrary sleeps and do not require identical pixels or bitwise physics outcomes across all architectures; software rendering is not substituted for target-GPU qualification.
Components, script bindings, command schemas and scene cases are tested as soon as those layers exist; incompatible/error configurations use isolated fixtures.
requirements.planned_fixture: TestingPolicyReview plus CI tier configuration; concrete renderer, audio and lifecycle fixtures are owned by their subsystem assignments and referenced above.
